input: What changed in the most recent FOMC statement compared with the previous one?

output.question: What changed in the most recent FOMC statement compared with the previous one?
output.answer: The latest statement, October 28, 2026, held the federal funds target at 3.75%–4.00%, whereas September 16 raised it by 0.25 percentage point to that range. ([federalreserve.gov](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/2026-press-fomc.htm)) Economic growth was described as “strong” rather than “solid.” ([federalreserve.gov](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20261028a.htm)) The inflation paragraph replaced September’s assurance about the hike’s effects with language saying additional information would help determine the appropriate policy stance. ([federalreserve.gov](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20261028a.htm)) The vote changed from 12–0 to 10–2, with Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack dissenting in favor of another quarter-point increase. ([federalreserve.gov](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20261028a.htm)) The remaining economic assessments, ample-reserves policy and commitment to price stability were unchanged. ([federalreserve.gov](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20261028a.htm))

key_facts.fact: As of November 10, 2026, the latest statement listed is October 28; its predecessor is September 16.
October held the target at 3.75%–4.00%, described growth as strong and introduced additional-information language.
September raised the target by 0.25 percentage point to 3.75%–4.00%, described growth as solid and said the action would support inflation's return to target.
October's vote was 10–2; Cook and Hammack preferred a quarter-point increase.
